q8.answer: Session state lives in Redis, a store both app instances share. Each session is a key named `sess:` plus the SHA-256 hash of the session ID, so whichever instance gets the request hashes the `sid` cookie and reads that key.

q9.answer: Each email's failed-login record is a Redis sorted set under `fails:` plus the hash of the email, holding the times of recent failures. The Lua script removes entries older than 10 minutes, adds the new attempt, and counts what remains, so only failures inside the sliding 10-minute window count.

q10.answer: On each protected request the server checks that the `sess:` key exists in Redis and that the current UTC time is before `absolute_expires_at`. If the session is still valid, it writes back an EXPIRE setting the TTL to the smaller of 30 minutes and the time left until absolute expiry.

q11.answer: The browser receives a 503 "Sign-in is unavailable right now. Try again in a few minutes." with no Set-Cookie, because the MULTI/EXEC transaction applies all three writes or none. The one exception is a dropped connection after Redis applied the transaction: the new session then exists with no cookie and expires by TTL.

q12.answer: No sweeper or cleanup job is needed: Redis deletes a session key when its 30-minute idle TTL passes, so abandoned sessions disappear on their own. The app also deletes a session at logout or when a request finds it past absolute expiry.
